Looking at this question, I need to recall information about H3.3K36R mutations in Drosophila and their effect on developmental viability (eclosure - emerging from the pupal case).

The H3.3K36R mutation replaces lysine 36 with arginine in the H3.3 histone variant, preventing the methylation (H3K36me) that is critical for transcription elongation and proper development.

From studies on Drosophila H3.3 variants, the H3.3K36R mutation causes significant developmental defects, resulting in reduced eclosure rates. The reported eclosure rate for H3.3K36R mutants is approximately 19%.
